body.codeblock: PRAGMA INTERRUPT { FAST | RAW | NORMAL | MVEC | [ cexpr ] }
body.p: This must be used within a procedure that takes no parameters. It defines the procedure as an interrupt entry point. Such a procedure is added to a chain of procedures executed whenever an interrupt hits. Once a procedure has been marked interrupt, it cannot be called directly by the program.

NORMAL, FAST, and RAW select how the register state is protected. The plain form (no word) is the same as NORMAL on the classic PIC targets and on PIC32 application-flash images. On PIC32MZ loader images a plain interrupt defaults to the fast shadow-register-set path, where the processor saves the registers instead of the generated code; FAST selects that path explicitly and RAW selects the software save and restore explicitly. RAW is required under PRAGMA ISA MICROMIPS, which has no encoding for the shadow-set instructions. On PIC32MX1/2 parts the shadow-register-set path does not exist, so a plain interrupt uses the software save and FAST is rejected with a diagnostic.

A number binds the procedure to a particular interrupt vector on targets that support multi-vector interrupts, for example PRAGMA INTERRUPT 12. The vector number must be in the range 0 to 255; the PIC32MX hardware table provides 64 entries, numbered 0 to 63.
MVEC enables the PIC32MX multi-vector interrupt table. It takes no argument and is used together with numbered PRAGMA INTERRUPT N statements.
